assumptions.source: World Bank WDI snapshots via outputs/stats/macro_inputs.json (tax-to-GDP of Tanzania 2024; benchmark peer_average, 2023)

tax_morale_model.status: RECALIBRATED (Block E2.3) to the observed adult TIN rate; effect sizes are ASSUMPTION uplifts; the naive sum is not a meaningful probability
tax_morale_model.definition: compliance probability = probability that an ADULT HOLDS A TIN (registration). The original code defines no event: it weights five driver scores (0-1) into an index and calls it a probability; the report (Fig 5.1, 'modeled compliance probability under the project's tax morale model') evaluates interventions aimed at TIN registration. Observed counterpart: FinScope 2023 weighted adult TIN rate.

observed_anchor.source: FinScope Tanzania 2023, weighted adult (16+) TIN rate, outputs/tables/tin_by_segment.csv (361 of 9,915 respondents)

calibration.alpha_target: baseline probability equals the observed adult TIN rate exactly (1 parameter, 1 target)
calibration.beta_target: least squares through the origin of beta x (index change of each intervention) on the log odds ratio the original linear model implied at its old baseline (6 solo interventions, 1 parameter)
calibration.uplift_sizes: the driver deltas (config tax_morale.effect.*) are unchanged ASSUMPTIONS; only their scale to log-odds is fitted

tax_morale_model.combination_rule: one active intervention: its solo odds ratio exp(beta x index change); two or more: the drivers' deltas are summed after multiplying each by tax_morale.combined_discount (0.6), capped at 1, then exp(beta x index change) (the rule that gives the combined effect of all six). Block E3.1: the agent and tier simulations multiply each agent's yearly registration odds by the odds ratio of the set of interventions that reach the agent

tax_morale_model.methodology: Weighted compliance probability model. Weights from Luttmer & Singhal (2014) and OECD Tax Morale report (2019). Baseline scores from FinScope Tanzania 2023 government trust and barrier variables.

agent_based_simulation.scenario: interventions (USSD TIN nudge for mobile-money users, civic tax education for urban adults 18+) switched on: yearly registration odds x the morale model's odds ratios
agent_based_simulation.status: CALIBRATED (Blocks E2.4 / E3.1): the no-intervention scenario reproduces TRA's registered-taxpayer trend 2017/18-2023/24 (RMSE 0.23 pp); intervention effects are the tax-morale model's odds ratios (ASSUMPTION uplifts)
agent_based_simulation.methodology: Vectorised agent-based simulation. 500,000 synthetic agents, 10 years. Age, mobile money, urban residence and the starting TIN status are a weighted resample of real FinScope Tanzania 2023 respondents' attributes (aggregate cells, data/processed/agent_cells.json) with the real-data targeting model's predicted propensities; income (ILFS 2024 earnings by age band) and trust and morale (Afrobarometer Round 8 by age band and urban/rural) are drawn from aggregate survey cell distributions. Yearly registration probability of a non-registered agent = conversion_rate x clip(trust, morale, income-rank and mobile-money terms + intercept); trust and morale are the agent's survey-based values and do not evolve (Block E3.1). Interventions multiply the agent's yearly registration odds by the tax-morale model's odds ratios (the same mechanism as Fig 5.1). Random seed: 42 for reproducibility.

no_intervention_scenario.status: CALIBRATED (Blocks E2.4 / E3.1): the no-intervention scenario reproduces TRA's registered-taxpayer trend 2017/18-2023/24 (RMSE 0.23 pp); intervention effects are the tax-morale model's odds ratios (ASSUMPTION uplifts)

digital_twin_baseline.scenario_note: A scenario of the model's own structure with ASSUMPTION inputs (policy strengths, trust and norm dynamics, penetration cap); not a forecast and not a measured outcome.

context_bot_active_mobile_money_accounts.note: context only (Block E3.3): BoT counts accounts, not persons; the twin uses FinScope's adult mobile-money users

digital_twin_baseline.registered_taxpayers_definition: registered_taxpayers = TRA's count of TIN registrations on the Mainland (a stock of registrations, individuals and entities, business and non-business, active or dormant; base: 6.27 million at the end of 2023/24, NBS Tax Statistics Report 2023/24 from TRA; series in data/processed/tra_registered_taxpayers.csv). It is NOT FinScope's 1.31 million ADULT TIN holders (a survey estimate of adults who say they hold a TIN) and the twin's compliance_rate (registered taxpayers divided by the adults of the Entry, Active and Enterprise stages) is therefore a registrations-per-adult ratio (adults = FinScope's adults 16+, grown with the population), not an adult TIN rate.
digital_twin_baseline.methodology: System dynamics digital twin. Interacting: households, MSMEs, mobile money, TRA, local governments. Policy changes propagate through trust dynamics, social norms, and registration feedback loops.

compliance_funnel.methodology: Compliance funnel using FinScope Tanzania 2023 microdata (n=9,915, weighted to 34,134,251 adults) for the Registration/TIN/Filing stages. Variables: MM composite, c27__1 (National ID), c27__13 (TIN). Revenue potential at 30% capture rate with 1.35x behavioral uplift. Extended (task #28) to cover the full funnel -- Registration -> TIN -> Filing -> Payment -> Audit -> Dispute -> Long-term Compliance: the Payment stage uses a real but AGGREGATE proxy (MoF's DOMESTIC reliefs rate for Q1 2023/24, a single quarter; the total rate incl. customs and excise is kept as a sensitivity case; not an individual-filer measurement); Audit, Dispute, and Long-term Compliance stages carry data_gap=True with count/pct/dropout=None because no individual-level transition-rate data exists in any source loaded into this project (Historical Audit Findings, task #12, was explicitly confirmed not publicly available) -- these stages are still populated with real qualitative/legal grounding (specific Act sections, real tribunal case-law topics) rather than omitted, but their quantitative fields are honestly left unset rather than estimated.

assumptions.source_uplift: Rwanda RRA + UK HMRC behavioral studies

assumptions.note: Kenya charges 0.3% excise on MM transfers

methodology_note: All figures calculated using Python formulas. No LLM estimates. Parameters from World Bank API, IMF DataMapper, OECD Revenue Statistics Africa, FinScope Tanzania 2023, and TRA Annual Reports. Behavioral uplift 1.35x from Rwanda RRA and UK HMRC behavioral tax studies. Monte Carlo: 1,000 iterations. Agent simulation: 500,000 synthetic citizens, 10 years. Random seed: 42.

tier_migration_simulation.status: CALIBRATED (Blocks E2.4 / E3.1): the no-intervention scenario reproduces TRA's registered-taxpayer trend 2017/18-2023/24 (RMSE 0.23 pp); intervention effects are the tax-morale model's odds ratios (ASSUMPTION uplifts)
tier_migration_simulation.methodology: Standalone simulation, separate from run_agent_based_simulation -- shares no mutable state with it. Same population-generation approach (weighted resample of real FinScope respondents' age, mobile money, urban residence and predicted TIN propensity, aggregate cells; income, trust and morale from ILFS / Afrobarometer aggregate cell distributions; random seed 42) plus two new per-agent dimensions: years_registered (increments while compliant) and a persistent filing-reliability trait correlated with trust and morale, redrawn with year-to-year noise rather than from scratch. Tier thresholds match exactly what the Enterprise-stage dashboard already displays.
